newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down after finmin statement.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down after finmin statement.

text.p: Thai stocks closed slightly lower on Tuesday as investors sold some large capitalised stocks after they termed as unclear the finance minister's statement on how to boost the economy, brokers said.
The SET index slipped 5.53 points to 867.23 on 3.2 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 0.53 point to 65.73.

"What Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on his plan to tackle economic problems could be interpretated as confirmation of bad news. For example, attempts by the present government to lower local interest rates were unclear, said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
The market had awaited anxiously to hear Amnuay, the new finance minister, detail his economic strategies.
Samart said foreign investors, who have mostly returned home for year-end holidays, were expected to reduce their weighting in the SET further on their return to the market.
"Local investors were active on selling in the market today as they probably found Amnuay's statement didn't give them enough confidence," said Samart.
Brokers said the market sentiment was already poor even before it opened this morning due to declines on the Wall Street overnight and several regional markets early.
